title: Household affordability motion defeated; mid-year budget update advanced
subtitle: Council conference policy for mayors, 2026 mid-year capital changes, arts council consultation and provincial cost pressures
overview: The Administration and Finance Committee recommended an updated Council Conference Policy that lets mayors attend conferences in their mayoral role and be reimbursed, with expenses routed through area municipalities to avoid double billing. It also recommended receiving the 2026 Mid-Year Update and amending the 2026 Capital Budget for various projects.

The committee defeated a motion for a "Household Affordability Framework" to be used each year in budget deliberations {{vote:m5}}. Councillors agreed affordability matters, but several worried about the scope, the expectations a framework would create, and extra staff work. Staff said they already use some affordability measures but would need outside data for others.

The committee also received an information report on arts council consultation findings. Staff plan to return in early 2027 with next steps, and the current arts fund administrator will continue through 2027. The next meeting is September 8, 2026.

decisions.detail: The committee recommended that Council approve the updated policy, including reimbursement for professional development and for mayors attending conferences as mayors {{vote:m2}}.
The committee recommended that Council receive the 2026 Mid-Year Update and amend the 2026 Capital Budget for various projects as set out in Appendix D {{vote:m3}}.
The committee defeated the motion directing staff to develop an annual framework on household affordability to inform budget deliberations {{vote:m5}}.
The committee received the Consent Agenda items for information and approved them {{vote:m1}}.

debate: Supporters of the affordability motion said inflation is only one measure of affordability. They said a baseline of income, housing, utility, food, transport and insurance indicators at the start of budgeting would give Council a fuller picture. The mover stressed it was not about capping or freezing the budget.

Several councillors said they already know affordability pressures and that data such as living wage figures exists. They argued another staff report was unnecessary and asked that no consultant money be spent.

Concerns about a framework included how to measure affordability fairly, the risk of creating expectations Council could not meet, and that a framework would bind Council once created. One councillor suggested staff first return with possible elements of a framework. Another asked that it show what the Region already does.

Some councillors asked that any analysis include police services budget and water and wastewater user rates, not only the regional tax levy. Staff said they could do this and could look at practices in peer regions.

On the mid-year report, councillors raised capital spending delivery and the share of the tax levy that goes to provincial responsibilities. Staff described a review of the gap between approved capital budgets and spending, and councillors linked the provincial costs to lobbying for a new fiscal arrangement.
